title: BOS #3: Activating the Zone
hook: A zone is only potential until BOS #3 closes through.

launchpad.outcome: Tell a potential zone from an active one, find BOS #3 on bullish and bearish charts, and recognize a zone that never activates.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What turns a potential zone into an active one?

takeaways: BOS #3 is a 5M candle close through the point Correction #2 pulled back from. It activates the zone.
An opposite-colour candle appearing is not activation. BOS #3 must occur.
BOS #3 isn’t an entry either. After it, you wait for the retest.

slides.headline: No BOS #3, no active zone.
slides.line: Correction #2 creates the zone. BOS (break of structure) #3 is the 5M close that makes it count.

slides.headline: Same box. Different status.
slides.line: A zone doesn’t activate just because the opposite-colour candle appeared.

versus.label: Potential zone
points: The entry model doesn’t apply yet.

versus.label: Active zone
points: A 5M candle closed through the point Correction #2 pulled back from.
Now you wait for price to return.

check.prompt: A bullish candle prints right after the last bearish candle of Correction #2. Is the demand zone active?

options.label: Yes, buyers have stepped in
options.feedback: A zone isn’t activated just because the opposite-colour candle appeared. BOS #3 must occur.

options.label: Not until BOS #3 closes
options.why: Right. BOS #3 is a 5M close above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. That’s what activates the zone.

slides.headline: Find BOS #3.
slides.line: The potential demand zone is drawn. Find the first 5M close above the high Correction #2 pulled back from.
slides.ask: Tap the candle that is BOS #3.
slides.why: That’s the first 5M candle to close above the high Correction #2 pulled back from.

after.caption: BOS #3. The demand zone is now active. Next, you wait for price to return.

slides.headline: Now the supply side.
slides.line: Find the first 5M close below the low Correction #2 pulled back from.
slides.ask: Tap the candle that is BOS #3.
slides.why: That’s the first 5M candle to close below the low Correction #2 pulled back from.

slides.kicker: Step 4 · A zone that never activates
slides.headline: Green candles. No BOS #3.
slides.line: Bullish example. Watch the potential zone, then what follows.

steps.caption: Bullish candles print, but none closes above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. No BOS #3. The zone stays potential.

check.prompt: Price keeps trading in the potential zone. Do you trade it?

options.label: Yes, it’s retesting the zone
options.feedback: It isn’t a retest. A retest only counts after BOS #3 has activated the zone, and BOS #3 never happened.

options.label: No, the zone was never activated
options.why: Right. Without BOS #3, the sequence is incomplete. No trade.

slides.headline: BOS #3 just closed. Now what?
slides.line: The zone is active and price is moving away from it.

check.prompt: BOS #3 just closed. What do you do?

options.label: Enter now, the sequence is complete
options.feedback: BOS #3 activates the zone. It isn’t an entry. The entry waits for price to return to the zone.

options.label: Wait for price to return to the zone
options.why: Right. After BOS #3, wait for the retest. Don’t chase.

slides.quote: A zone without BOS #3 is just a box on a chart.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what is the difference between a potential zone and an active zone?
slides.modelAnswer: A potential zone is created by Correction #2, from its last opposite-colour candle. It only becomes active when BOS #3 occurs: a 5M candle close through the point Correction #2 pulled back from. An opposite-colour candle appearing isn’t enough. If BOS #3 never happens, the zone never activates and there is no trade. Even after BOS #3, I wait for price to return to the zone.
